prompt.context: Your client is CNB Movies, a national movie theater company with $2 billion in annual revenue. In recent years, movie theaters have seen record high demand for Marvel and DC Comics movies, and CNB is considering ways to capitalize on this demand. One option is to offer 24-hour opening weekend screenings for these movies.
prompt.question: The company has hired you to advise on the decision. Should they offer this 24-hour opening weekend experience?

clarifying_info.q: When does CNB want to implement this?

clarifying_info.a: Opening weekend starts Thursday night and ends Sunday at 11:59 PM — that is 3 nights.

clarifying_info.q: How many theaters would this apply to?
clarifying_info.a: CNB wants to test one theater first. If successful, they would roll out to all 400 theaters in the US.

clarifying_info.q: Are any competitors currently offering this?
clarifying_info.a: None of CNB's competitors currently offer this experience.

clarifying_info.q: Does CNB have the capital to finance this?
clarifying_info.a: Yes, CNB Movies is capable of financing this on its own.

exhibits.title: Expected Seat Utilization Per Showing
exhibits.shows: A bar chart showing expected seat utilization (as a percentage) broken down by audience segment — Children, Adults, and Seniors — for three showtimes: 12:00 AM, 3:00 AM, and 6:00 AM. Each theater has 300 seats.

exhibits.title: Daily Cost Structure Per Theater
exhibits.shows: A table listing current daily costs per theater across four categories: Staff, Concessions, Concession Maintenance, and Projector Maintenance.

framework: Revenue: Ticket sales (adults vs. children/seniors at different showtimes) + Concession revenue
Costs: Staff (cashiers, ticket checkers, cleaning, security) + Concession COGS + Concession maintenance + Projector maintenance + Utilities
Incremental profit = Total new revenue – Total new costs over the 3-night weekend

Risk/qualitative factors: Competitive response, capital maintenance risk from 24-hr projector use, premium pricing potential, opportunity cost of alternative projects, concession fluctuations at odd hours

questions.prompt: Using Exhibit 1, calculate total ticket revenue per night across all three overnight showtimes.
questions.guidance: Candidate should compute revenue at each showtime using the formula: Revenue = (seats) × [(% children × $10) + (% adults × $15) + (% seniors × $10)]. Then sum across all three showtimes.

math.setup: Ticket Rev @ time = 300 × [(% children × $10) + (% adults × $15) + (% seniors × $10)]

questions.prompt: Calculate total concession revenue per night. Average concession spend is $10 per person.
questions.guidance: Candidate must apply the $10/person concession figure to total attendance at each showtime (derived from seat utilization rates). Strong candidate proactively asks about other revenue streams beyond tickets.

math.setup: Concessions = $10 × total attendees across all three showtimes

questions.prompt: What is total revenue for the entire opening weekend?
questions.guidance: Candidate must recall that opening weekend = 3 nights (Thursday, Friday, Saturday nights) and multiply nightly total by 3.

math.setup: Total weekend revenue = (ticket revenue + concession revenue per night) × 3 nights

questions.prompt: Using Exhibit 2 and the cost increase assumptions, calculate total incremental costs for the opening weekend under the new 24-hour model.
questions.guidance: Candidate should apply the percentage increases to each cost line item provided in the exhibit, compute the new daily total, and multiply by 3 nights. Cost increase assumptions (provided by interviewer alongside Exhibit 2): Staff +50%, Concessions +50%, Concession Maintenance +25%, Projector Maintenance +10%.

math.setup: New daily cost per line = Current cost × (1 + increase%). Total weekend cost = new daily total × 3.

questions.prompt: What is the incremental profit from the 24-hour opening weekend model for one theater?
questions.guidance: Simple subtraction of total weekend costs from total weekend revenue. Strong candidate also notes the profit margin.

math.setup: Incremental profit = Total revenue – Total costs

brainstorming.prompt: What are some additional factors that CNB should consider before making their final decision?

categories.name: Internal / Financial
ideas: Sensitivity analysis on demand and cost assumptions — projections may vary significantly by theater and geography
Upfront marketing costs to promote 24-hour screenings
Whether to roll out to all 400 theaters or a targeted subset based on market analysis
Capital risk from running projectors 24 hours (accelerated depreciation, unplanned maintenance)

categories.name: Customer & Market
ideas: Risk of cannibalizing existing customer base (customers shifting from prime-time to overnight showings)
Customer/demographic analysis by region — late-night demand may differ by city
Determine which blockbusters qualify for the 24-hour model; not all movies will drive demand

categories.name: Competitive & Strategic
ideas: How will competition react? First-mover advantage vs. risk of quick imitation
If CNB does not act, could a competitor launch first and capture market share?
Potential to price overnight tickets at a premium given novelty and exclusivity
Long-term brand and word-of-mouth marketing benefits

recommendation: CNB Movies should implement the 24-hour opening weekend experience. The expected incremental profit is $10,800 per theater per opening weekend, representing a 22% profit margin.
The experience also provides CNB with a first-mover competitive advantage for high-grossing blockbusters, with no current competitor offering this option.
risks: Demand and cost assumptions may not hold — further analysis needed before full rollout
Projections will vary by theater and geography; a single pilot may not be representative
A movie underperforming at the box office would significantly reduce attendance and revenue
Running projectors 24 hours may accelerate maintenance costs beyond the 10% projection
next_steps: Develop a targeted marketing strategy to promote the 24-hour experience
Run sensitivity analysis on attendance and cost assumptions across different scenarios
Identify optimal rollout strategy: select pilot theaters by region and demographics
Define criteria for which movies qualify (e.g., expected box office threshold) and which markets to prioritize
